rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Recombinant DNA (rDNA) technology follows 7 detailed steps: isolate the gene, cut it with restriction enzymes, ligate it into a vector, transform a host cell, select the transformants, express the gene, and harvest the product. Plasmids are the most common vectors (ori, selectable marker, MCS). E. coli is the standard host for simple proteins; yeast and mammalian cells are used for complex, glycosylated proteins.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
rDNA: isolate → cut (restriction enzyme) → ligate (DNA ligase) → transform → select → express → harvest
Plasmid: ori + selectable marker + MCS + high copy number
Insulin: human gene → E. coli → fermentation → purification → insulin

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Restriction enzymes CUT DNA at specific sequences; DNA ligase JOINS DNA fragments; they are different tools.  ·  A plasmid is a small circular DNA molecule used as a VECTOR; it is NOT the gene of interest itself.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects the 7 rDNA steps clearly, with the role of each tool (restriction enzyme, ligase, vector, host).  ·  The plasmid vector structure (ori, selectable marker, MCS, copy number) is a common exam point.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: rDNA steps: isolate → cut (EcoRI) → ligate → transform → select (ampicillin) → express → harvest (insulin).  ·  Plasmid vector: pBR322 (ori, ampR, tetR, MCS); pUC19 (lacZ for blue-white screening).

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: rDNA 7 steps  ·  Restriction enzymes + ligase  ·  Plasmid vectors (ori, marker, MCS)  ·  Host cells (E. coli, yeast, mammalian)

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: rDNA: 7 steps (isolate, cut, ligate, transform, select, express, harvest).  ·  Vectors: plasmids, phages, cosmids, BACs, YACs; features: ori, selectable marker, MCS.  ·  Host cells: E. coli (prokaryotic), yeast (eukaryotic), mammalian cells.  ·  Medical: insulin (1982), vaccines (HBV, HPV), monoclonal antibodies, gene therapy.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Recombinant human insulin was the first biotech drug approved for human use (1982).  ·  The HPV vaccine, derived from recombinant virus-like particles, can prevent cervical cancer.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: How is human insulin produced using rDNA?  ·  What is the use of Bt crops in pest management?  ·  Discuss the ethical issues of GMOs.

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: Insulin production: human insulin gene → E. coli → fermentation → purification → insulin.  ·  Hepatitis B vaccine: yeast expressing HBsAg protein → purified → vaccine.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: The use of microbial biotechnology is described below: 1.  ·  In Medicine: The concept of microbial biotechnology is used in human and veterinary medicine by the following ways: a.  ·  Antibiotics: Antibiotics are substances obtained from microorganisms that help in controlling different types of diseases.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: They are obtained from different types of microorganisms.  ·  Vaccines: Vaccines are the substances derived from microorganisms used to immunize against disease.  ·  CRISPR: guide RNA + Cas9 → cut DNA → repair → desired change

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Agricultural: Bt crops, herbicide-tolerant crops, tissue culture, biofertilisers.  ·  Industrial: enzymes, bioremediation, biofuels, biogas.  ·  Gene therapy (correct a faulty gene) vs gene editing (CRISPR tool).
